newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates near flat, liquidity high.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates near flat, liquidity high.

text.p: Croatian interbank rates were steady to lower on Tuesday in slow trade, dealers said.
"Supply today is very good but is not being matched by demand as banks enjoy good liquidity," a dealer said.
Morning trade totalled 16.5 million kuna ($2.6 million), leaving some 50 million kuna on the supply side.
Call money loans granted at a lower than usual 7.0 percent and the regular 8.0 percent, accounted for 7.5 million of the mornings' transactions.
One three-day loan was granted at 8.0 percent, while one-month deals were struck at 9.5, 10 and 13 percent. Two-month borrowings were made at 17 and 18 percent.
Commercial banks had 5.5 million kuna in outstanding Lombard loans, flat from the weekend. No new loans were taken.

Overnight trade on Monday was put at 5.7 million kuna, of which five million was used by one bank to maintain its mandatory reserves. The banking sector ended on Monday with 693 million kuna in its accounts, up 63 million from the weekend. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom 385-1-4557075 ($ = 6.377 Croatian Kuna)
